existing_coverage: SO_PEERCRED returns connection-time peer credentials and does not identify executable or distinguish same-UID processes.
MCP tool annotations are untrusted unless the server itself is trusted; HTTP transport authorization guidance is already catalogued.
E12 already distinguishes managed enrollment, active status, actual checks, and heartbeat freshness; E13 covers endpoint-local bypass.
duplicate_check.new_scope: Use official upstream designs to compare client-reported heartbeat trust, Unix-socket workload identity, atomic epoch/CAS updates, and database transaction races. This is reference analysis, not a claim that those components are implemented here.

references.title: Kubernetes Leases and node heartbeat design
references.read_scope: Versioned Kubernetes Lease concept page: node heartbeat renewTime and control-plane availability interpretation; pinned kubelet nodelease helper source reviewed for how node Lease renewal is issued.
references.sha256_scope: UTF-8 bytes returned by raw.githubusercontent.com for pkg/kubelet/util/nodelease.go at the pinned commit; docs page itself was read in the browser and was not locally archived.
references.official_claim: Kubernetes represents node heartbeat with a coordination.k8s.io Lease; kubelet updates spec.renewTime and the control plane uses that timestamp to assess Node availability. The Lease is a liveness signal in a control plane that also has node identity and authorization boundaries.
references.application: For LOCAL-RISK-08 and E12, keep liveness freshness as an independently expiring admission condition, but do not treat a recent client heartbeat as proof that local firewall/profile checks are true. Bind accepted updates to the enrolled device identity and expected policy/configuration generation; test stale/replayed heartbeats and a healthy timestamp paired with failed or missing checks. Compare evidence from the server-side stored observation with the client claim.
references.limitations: Kubernetes Lease semantics are not an endpoint attestation mechanism. A recent Lease proves a recent accepted update under Kubernetes API identity/authorization, not measurement of kernel policy or binary integrity. Kubernetes NodeRestriction and its control-plane model are not present by merely copying the renewTime pattern.

references.title: SPIRE agent Workload API and peer-credential attestation
references.read_scope: Pinned agent documentation: Workload API is served through a configured Unix socket; workload is implicitly attested through socket peer credentials; contrasted with delegated identity and experimental broker APIs, including their distinct authentication/configuration boundaries.
references.sha256_scope: UTF-8 bytes returned by raw.githubusercontent.com for doc/spire_agent.md at the pinned commit.
references.official_claim: SPIRE documents peer credentials as part of Workload API caller attestation. Its separate broker endpoint uses mTLS with an allowlist and allowed reference types; the document explicitly identifies that broker API as experimental in this release line.
references.application: For LOCAL-RISK-10 and the Unix SO_PEERCRED boundary, use this as a comparator for an identity chain: socket peer credentials are an input to an attestor/selector decision, not a raw UID equality check that grants all same-UID processes the same assurance. A test design can vary PID/UID/registered selector and confirm identity issuance or denial, then separately test revocation/expiry of issued identity before admission. Keep privileged service identity and caller identity distinct.
references.limitations: SPIRE requires a configured trust domain, registration entries, attestor plugins, agent server, and identity lifecycle; it is not a drop-in local MCP sandbox. The cited claim does not make Linux peer credentials proof against a privileged host/root attacker or prove arbitrary executable integrity. Experimental broker API guidance must not be generalized as stable Workload API behavior.

references.title: etcd transaction compare-and-swap API
references.read_scope: Versioned transaction API explanation: atomic If/Then/Else operations and compare predicates; pinned RPC schema reviewed for TxnRequest compare/success/failure structure and lease/transaction API boundaries.
references.sha256_scope: UTF-8 bytes returned by raw.githubusercontent.com for api/etcdserverpb/rpc.proto at the pinned commit.
references.official_claim: etcd Txn evaluates comparisons and executes one of the success or failure operation lists atomically. The revision/version comparison model can guard a state transition against a concurrent writer.
references.application: For admission freshness, epoch/revoke, and database-race scenarios, derive a concurrency test pattern: compare the observed device or credential generation and update/revoke it in one atomic transaction; race issue/refresh against revoke and require exactly one valid post-race state. If the current PostgreSQL store remains authoritative, implement the equivalent in its transaction/conditional-update semantics rather than adding etcd as a dependency.
references.limitations: This documents an etcd primitive, not an authorization policy or a guarantee that the current solution uses etcd. Compare-and-swap is only effective if all relevant writers share the same key/revision discipline and failure path; it does not itself expire cached credentials or invalidate tokens at downstream consumers.

references.title: PostgreSQL explicit row locking and application consistency
references.version: PostgreSQL 17.11 source tag REL_17_11; PostgreSQL 17 versioned documentation
references.read_scope: Versioned docs: SELECT FOR UPDATE row-lock behavior, concurrent writer wait/re-read behavior, lock duration, and application consistency caveats. Pinned MVCC documentation source reviewed for transaction isolation and write-conflict semantics.
references.sha256_scope: UTF-8 bytes returned by raw.githubusercontent.com for doc/src/sgml/mvcc.sgml at the pinned commit.
references.official_claim: PostgreSQL row-level FOR UPDATE locks conflict with updates/deletes/other row locks until the transaction ends; a blocked command can continue against an updated row. Application consistency guidance warns that locking alone does not permanently prevent a later update after the lock holder commits; a required state transition must be performed while holding the lock, or otherwise use a correctly scoped atomic write.
references.application: The solution uses PostgreSQL for OAuth refresh-token and managed endpoint state. Add race cases around the actual transaction boundary: two concurrent issue/refresh requests versus refresh-family revocation or managed device epoch change; ensure a stale generation cannot commit after revocation, both requests cannot consume the same one-time refresh state, and rollback leaves no partial token-family update. Inspect the existing advisory family lock and row lock in full_stack_lab/gateway/app/idp.py, then assert committed rows and downstream managed_failure behavior rather than response codes alone.
references.limitations: A row lock is not a process or endpoint boundary, and does not automatically bind authorization to the row being locked. Correctness still depends on every writer using the same transaction protocol, handling serialization/deadlock errors, and keeping external side effects outside or idempotent around the database commit.

findings.finding: Freshness and truth are separate properties.
findings.verification: Normal: active enrolled device, fresh heartbeat, matching device epoch and current policy hash pass managed admission. Negative: stale heartbeat, replayed older epoch, malformed/missing checks, or fresh heartbeat paired with a failed enforcement check is denied or quarantined; explicitly test whether the current server actually rejects that reported failed check rather than infer it from freshness. Independent effect: wait past heartbeat TTL while token expiry remains later and verify managed admission fails.

findings.finding: Kernel-reported peer credentials are useful only when consumed by an identity/attestation policy; UID-only comparison remains a shared-UID trust boundary.
findings.verification: Normal: enrolled user process connects through the intended socket and receives only its own bound credential context. Negative: wrong UID, unauthorized PID/selector, stale/revoked workload identity, or same-UID unauthorized process is not elevated by the socket check alone. Independent effect: verify OS socket mode/owner and AppArmor/service restrictions separately; do not infer process isolation from SO_PEERCRED.

findings.finding: Revocation epochs and freshness checks need a single atomic compare-and-transition boundary; otherwise concurrent refresh/issue can race revocation.
findings.verification: Normal: generation-matched refresh and policy checks commit under their intended locks. Negative: race refresh/reuse with family revoke, or managed admission with device revoke/epoch change; stale-generation requests must not remain usable after the revoke boundary. Independent effect: assert one refresh winner, old family rows revoked, device state/epoch reflected by the next managed_failure check, no partial successor rows, and repeat after injected rollback/deadlock/serialization retry. The source already contains a family advisory lock and refresh-row FOR UPDATE; this is a proposal to verify interactions and revoke/admission ordering, not a statement that the lock is absent.

findings.finding: Tool/process inventory, health claims, and protocol metadata are evidence inputs rather than enforcement boundaries.
findings.verification: Confirm that a matching process name, claimed healthy status, or recent heartbeat alone cannot activate managed privileges. Verify a separately enforced identity, policy hash, fresh generation, and OS boundary; preserve explicit unknown/unverified state where those proofs are absent.
